name: Valentin Borisovich Aleskovskii
summary: Soviet chemist and professor who proposed the 'framework' hypothesis and co-founded the molecular layering method.

name: Stanislav Ivanovich Kol'tsov
summary: Soviet chemist and graduate student of Aleskovskii who co-developed the molecular layering method.

name: Leningrad Technological Institute by Lensovet
aliases: St. Petersburg State Technological Institute (Technical University)
summary: Russian technical university where Aleskovskii studied and worked for most of his career.

name: Leningrad State University
summary: Russian university where Aleskovskii served as rector and founded a department.

name: Naval Research Institute
summary: Research institute in Leningrad where Aleskovskii worked as a research fellow after graduation.

name: Academy of Sciences of the USSR
summary: Soviet academy of which Aleskovskii became a corresponding member.

name: Supreme Soviet of the Russian Federation
summary: Legislative body of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic where Aleskovskii was a member.

name: Mary
summary: City in Turkmenistan where Aleskovskii was born.

name: Molecular Layering
summary: Gas-phase layer by layer deposition technology developed by Aleskovskii and Kol'tsov.

name: Framework hypothesis
summary: Theoretical concept proposed by Aleskovskii regarding the chemical structure of solids.

name: Department of Chemistry of Solids
aliases: Department of Chemical Engineering of Materials and Electronics Products
Department of Chemical Nanotechnology and Electronics Engineering Materials
summary: Department at LTI founded by Aleskovskii in 1967.

name: Department of Solid State Chemistry
summary: Department at LSU organized by Aleskovskii in 1977.

name: Chemical assembly of materials
summary: Inter-university scientific and technical program founded in 1978 under Aleskovskii's supervision.
